thesis: MRVL beat Q2 FY27 estimates on both revenue ($2.74B record, +37% YoY) and EPS ($0.94 non-GAAP) and raised Q3 guidance for a second straight quarter on 46% YoY data-center growth, yet shares dropped ~6% in after-hours trading following the print. The negative reaction despite a genuine beat-and-raise suggests the bar was already priced in after the stock's ~187% YTD run, not that the business deteriorated -- but that same dynamic makes a fresh long entry risky right into an active post-earnings selloff.
invalidation: shares stabilize or reclaim the pre-earnings ~$241 level in the next 1-2 sessions, confirming the market ultimately read the beat-and-raise as positive rather than as a valuation reset

thesis: STX has fallen roughly 19% over the past two weeks (-9.2% on 8/18, -7.9% on 8/21, -6.5% on 8/24) after analysts warned its record 52.7% non-GAAP gross margin reflects temporary HDD industry pricing power and product mix rather than a durable HAMR technology moat, compounded by disclosed customer concentration (~14% of FY26 revenue from a single hyperscaler) and large CEO/CFO share sales on 8/21 ($15.4M and $7.7M respectively). A $175M securities-fraud settlement over alleged concealment of Huawei export-law violations has a Final Settlement Hearing scheduled for 11/17/2026, within the next ~90 days.
invalidation: margin durability is confirmed with a stabilized gross-margin print next quarter and shares recover toward pre-selloff levels without further negative litigation or customer-concentration news
